state:
Patient portal thread — Dana M. and Nurse Kelly

Dana, 10:02am: Hi, I've been having some heart palpitations on and off since yesterday, feels like fluttering for a few seconds. Not painful, just noticeable.
Nurse Kelly, 10:20am: Thanks for reaching out. How often is this happening, and do you have any chest pain, dizziness, or shortness of breath with it?
Dana, 10:35am: Maybe 5-6 times yesterday and twice so far today. No chest pain or dizziness that I've noticed. I did have a lot of coffee yesterday and less sleep than usual.
Nurse Kelly, 10:50am: Ok, that's helpful. Given no chest pain, dizziness, or shortness of breath, and the caffeine/sleep pattern, this sounds most consistent with benign palpitations related to caffeine and fatigue rather than anything dangerous. That said, please keep tracking episodes and let us know if anything changes.
Dana, 11:15am: Update, sorry — just had a longer episode, felt like almost 30 seconds this time, and I did feel a little lightheaded for a moment during it.
Nurse Kelly, 11:22am: Thanks for the update, that changes things a bit. A 30-second episode with lightheadedness is longer and more significant than what you described before. I'd like you to come in today for an ECG rather than wait — can you come in this afternoon, or if it happens again with lightheadedness before then, please go to urgent care.
Dana, 11:30am: Ok, I can come in at 2pm. Will do if it happens again before then.
Nurse Kelly, 11:31am: Perfect, see you at 2, and please message us again if anything changes before then.
Dana, 1:45pm: Just finished the ECG, wanted to update the thread — Dr. Osei said the ECG itself looks normal, no signs of a dangerous rhythm, but she wants me to wear a 48-hour heart monitor to catch what's happening during an actual episode, since palpitations often look normal on a single snapshot ECG done between episodes.
Nurse Kelly, 1:52pm: That's a very reasonable next step and good news that the snapshot ECG was normal. We'll get the monitor set up before you leave today. In the meantime, please still message us right away, or go to urgent care, if you get another episode with lightheadedness like this morning's, don't wait for the monitor to explain it after the fact if it feels different or worse.
Dana, 1:55pm: Understood, will do. Thanks for taking this seriously and not just brushing off the caffeine explanation once things changed.

state:
Patient portal thread — Marcus P. and Nurse Team

Marcus, Monday 9:00am: Hi, quick question about my new blood pressure medication (lisinopril) — is it normal to feel a little dizzy when standing up the first few days?
Nurse Team, Monday 11:30am: Hi Marcus, yes, mild lightheadedness when standing is a known side effect for the first 1-2 weeks as your body adjusts. Try standing up slowly, and let us know if it's severe or doesn't improve.
Marcus, Wednesday 8:15am: Thanks, it was fine for a couple days. Today though, I stood up and got so dizzy I had to sit right back down, and my vision went a bit gray for a few seconds.
Nurse Team, Wednesday 9:00am: Thanks for the update. A brief grayout with standing can still be part of the adjustment, but let's keep an eye on it — can you check your blood pressure at home if you have a cuff, both sitting and standing?
Marcus, Wednesday 9:40am: Just checked — sitting it's 118/76, but standing after a minute it dropped to 84/54 and I felt the dizziness again, plus my heart was pounding really fast.
Nurse Team, Wednesday 9:50am: That drop (118/76 to 84/54) with symptoms is more than the usual adjustment — that's a significant orthostatic drop. Please stop taking the lisinopril for now and come in today so we can check you in person; if you feel faint or can't stay seated safely before your appointment, call 911 instead.
Marcus, Wednesday 9:52am: Ok, I can come in at 1pm, will call the office if it gets worse before then.
Marcus, Wednesday 1:40pm: Just left the appointment. Dr. Osei switched me from lisinopril to a different blood pressure medication (amlodipine) that's less likely to cause this kind of drop, and wants me to check my blood pressure at home twice a day for the next week and log it in the portal.
Nurse Team, Wednesday 1:50pm: Thanks for the update, glad the visit went well. We'll keep an eye on your logged readings on our end too. Please still reach out or call 911 if you get any more grayouts or dizziness on the new medication, but this kind of switch usually resolves the orthostatic drop within a day or two.
Marcus, Thursday 8:00am: Quick update, no dizziness at all yesterday evening or this morning on the new medication, and my standing blood pressure log looks much more stable. Thanks for catching this quickly.
